issues.title: Bug: `worker: true` returns malformed parse results in Vite v8 production builds
issues.body:
After upgrading a project from Vite v7 to v8, PapaParse parsing breaks in production builds when using `worker: true`.

The same code works correctly:

* in development mode
* in Vite v7
* when `worker: false`

## Expected behavior

Parsing a CSV with:

```js
Papa.parse(csv, {
  header: true,
  worker: true,
})
```

should return parsed rows in `data`.

Example:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "property": "reportName",
      "value": "Example",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Actual behavior

The parsed result is malformed:

* `data` contains only `null` values
* the actual row contents appear inside `meta.fields`

Example output:

```json
{
  "data": [null, null, null],
  "errors": [],
  "meta": {
    "fields": [
      "property",
      "value",
      "type",
      ["reportName", "Example", "string"]
    ]
  }
}
```

This later causes runtime crashes because the application expects parsed row objects.

## Notes

What I know so far:

* Regression appeared after upgrading Vite v7 → v8
* Only happens in production builds
* Does not happen in development mode
* Only happens when `worker: true`
* Setting `worker: false` fixes the issue

## Reproduction repository

I created a minimal reproduction repository [here](https://github.com/milachae/papaparse-worker-test).

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
npm install
npm run build
python3 -m http.server 3000
```

Then open:

```txt
http://localhost:3000
```

comments.author: bbiallowons

comments.body:
Adding a tested Terser option alongside the esbuild workaround above. With an independent two-row, same-origin `download: true` reproduction, I get these Chrome production-build results:

| Vite / PapaParse | Default minifier, Worker | Terser 5.51.2, Worker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8.0.14 / 5.5.3 | Null rows; row arrays appended to `meta.fields` | Correct rows and headers |
| 8.2.2 / 5.7.0 | `skipEmptyLines` Worker exception; no completion within 4 seconds | Correct rows and headers |

Disabling minification also passed for both pairs; the main-thread control passed in all six builds.

For the Terser configuration:

```sh
npm install --save-dev --save-exact terser@5.51.2
```

Merge this into the existing Vite config, keeping the framework plugins and other settings:

```js
build: {
  minify: 'terser',
}
```

Keep `worker: true`, rebuild, and test the served production output. This changes the app's JavaScript minifier, so check the complete application before adopting it.

I also put the [standalone reproduction checks and configuration guide](https://github.com/tevinch/data-shape-kit/tree/main/examples/papaparse-vite-worker) in a free MIT example. Its current-version Terser build passed four fixtures in both execution modes, comparing complete data, parse errors and expected fields, including leading zeros, Unicode and quoted CRLF.

These results are for the released packages above. #1145 is the proposed upstream fix; I have not tested that patch. Once a fix ships, rerun the production comparison before keeping a minifier workaround.

issues.title: Four streaming defects: chunk-boundary UTF-8 corruption, cached line-ending guess, header dedupe on resume, and no backpressure under pause()
issues.body:
Each item below has an offline reproduction. Note your CI is green at this commit, so none of this is visible from the suite as it stands.

- **Multi-byte UTF-8 split across a chunk boundary decodes to `U+FFFD`** (`papaparse.js:891`). Any non-ASCII file parsed with chunking can silently lose characters.
- **The line ending is guessed from a truncated first chunk and then cached for the whole file** (`papaparse.js:1091`). With `chunkSize: 1024` on a CRLF file this leaves a stray `\r` on every last field, with no error raised and a correct row count, so it looks like clean data.
- **Header dedupe re-runs on every resumed row and rewrites data in place** (`papaparse.js:1750`). This reproduces issues #985 and #998 verbatim.
- **`pause()` applies no backpressure** (`papaparse.js:846-856`). 100% of the stream buffers while paused; a 400 MB file under `--max-old-space-size=128` dies with `FATAL ERROR: JavaScript heap out of memory`, where the unpaused control completes at 78 MB RSS.

Two things I checked that are **not** broken, so nobody wastes time on them: quoted fields spanning chunk boundaries are exact at every chunk size across four corpora, and the pause/resume regression test that fails on Windows is a timer-resolution artifact (`setTimeout(3)` costs ~15.8 ms there, and `resume` schedules one timer per row), not a deadlock.

I have a patch taking the suite to 248 passing / 0 failing with lint clean. Several existing open PRs (#1099, #909, #1107, #989, #1017, #1131) cover adjacent ground and predate this. Happy to open a PR or leave it here.

comments.body:
Thanks - opened one per issue, each with a regression test that fails on master:

- #1133 multi-byte character split across a chunk boundary
- #1134 line ending guessed from a truncated chunk
- #1135 header de-duplication re-running on every resumed row
- #1136 `pause()` applying no backpressure to the source

Each branch is cut from master independently, so they can be reviewed and merged in any order, and all six pairwise merges are clean. Every PR body carries the red-green output showing the new test failing before the fix and passing after.

I left the remaining findings out of these four deliberately: the `meta.cursor` regression, the swallowed stream error, the missing `.gitattributes` and the `StringStreamer.prototype` self-assignment are lower severity and would only add review load here. Happy to send any of them separately if you want them.

One note on #1136: the `StringStreamer.prototype` self-assignment had to come along, because reverting just that line makes the existing tests fail with `TypeError: self.streamer.pause is not a function`. It is called out in that PR body.

The pre-existing bug #636 timeout still fails on all four branches, exactly as it does on master. It is a Windows timer-resolution artifact and I have not touched it here.
